Subject: Unexpected embed-unit jump on May invoice — need trace

Hi Hannah,

We just received our May invoice and theres a ~48% spike in embeddings units compared to our normal baseline. Weve checked our own deploys and sampling rates and nothing changed on our side. Can you help with a session-level breakdown or traces so we can pinpoint whether this came from a replay, orphaned backfill, or an attribution change on Redwoods side?

What wed find most helpful: a small sample (1-2 hours) of session traces that show request id, timestamp, model variant, region, and the embed-unit attribution. Ideally CSV.

Were trying to avoid opening a collection hold but need evidence to reconcile with our finance team. Happy to jump on a quick call if that helps — available 10:00-12:00 CEST today.

Thanks,
Alex
VP Engineering | QuickFin Inc.

Subject: Re: Request for session-level traces — quick forensic notes

Hannah / Marissa — attaching the sample export (telemetry CSV) and a short engineers write-up (engineer_analysis.pdf). Summary of findings: 

- Scope: pulled session traces for 2028-05-14 01:00:00 UTC through 2028-05-14 03:00:00 UTC for QuickFin tenant id qf-prod-77.
- Root cause candidate: a mis-tagged staging API key was present in prefixed routing for a 40-minute window (01:21-02:01 UTC) and caused duplicated attribution to the production tenant. The tokenization and embed-unit calculation pipeline recorded the requests twice during a rolling replay.
- Impact: ~35% of the observed spike maps to the mis-tagged key window; the remaining delta is smaller bursts from a scheduled backfill job that did not respect tenant throttles and was rerouted to prod for 9 minutes.
- Evidence included: request_id, timestamp, api_key_label, model_variant, ttl_ms, embed_units, region.

Attachments (stubs): quickfin_sample-telemetry.csv (3.2MB), engineer_analysis.pdf (1.1MB).

Notes: We recommend a provisional credit for the duplicated window while we harden routing checks and add an ingest guard. We can propose a credit equal to the usage attributable to the mis-tagged key window; Marissa, happy for you to propose the exact credit figure to Alex / finance.

Ben
Senior Billing Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Reconcile embed-unit variance — provisional credit and next steps

Hi Alex — thanks for your patience. We pulled together the bundle Ben referenced and confirmed the two contributing causes. Im proposing the following: 

1) Provisional credit: were offering a provisional credit of EUR 12,800, which covers all usage we can confidently attribute to the mis-tagged staging key window (01:21-02:01 UTC) plus the short backfill reroute. This will appear as a credit line on your July invoice unless you prefer immediate offset against the May charge.

2) Evidence package: attached are the CSV and engineer write-up (same attachments Ben called out). They include request_id, timestamp (UTC), api_key_label, model_variant, embed_units, and region.

3) Long-term fixes: engineering will add an ingest guard (api_key validation) and an hourly reconciliation job to detect duplicate attributions within tenant namespaces. Karthik will lead the rollout and has estimated a two-week fix window for the guard.

If that credit path works for you, please reply with authorization to apply it, or propose alternate handling (refund, invoice offset). Happy to set a short call with finance if helpful — were available tomorrow 09:00-11:00 CEST.

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
